Subject: Clearsky Health — hosting constraints & residency decision path

Hi Emma (and team),

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard, confirm assumptions, and align next steps so procurement/engineering have clear inputs. I kept this high level — flag anything I mischaracterized.

Summary of pain points / drivers
- Regulatory: Clearsky needs EU-resident processing for PHI-adjacent telemetry; certain product flows may require full data residency inside EU (no cross-border tokenization).
- Security: A subset of workloads will require air-gapped or private-only endpoints (no outbound public egress) due to partner PHI contracts.
- Network ops constraints: customer-managed VPN + private peering only; NAT/Gateway egress will be an exception and needs justification.
- Latency/throughput: real-time triage pipelines expect 100–200ms LLM latency at P95 for short prompts; bursty batch jobs for inference retraining are fine to schedule off-peak.
- Procurement/controls: SOC2 evidence + attestation on data handling, and contract language around data deletion/retention windows.

Assumptions we made (please confirm)
1) You want Redwood Private deployed inside Clearsky VPC (customer-managed) with no inference traffic leaving the VPC except to approved endpoints.
2) Certificates and KMS will be customer-managed (we will integrate with your KMS/HSM).
3) Model hosting can be split: sensitive flows pinned to air-gapped nodes; lower-risk flows may hit a dedicated but internet-connected pool.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Emma: confirm whether the procurement team requires a vendor security questionnaire or a full SOC2 package copy as a starting point (procurement email in cc).
- Clearsky infra: can you share the basic network diagram (subnets, NAT/GW, peering endpoints) or allow a short call with your NetOps? I attached a quick sketch to annotate. (attachment: clearsky-network-sketch.png)
- Redwood: we’ll send our on-prem/VPC checklist and a short runbook template for air-gap installs by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed timeline
- Week 1: Technical discovery (NetOps + Security) — schedule 60m deep-dive
- Week 2: Proof-of-concept scoping (scope: one model + ingress for triage pipeline)
- Week 3–4: Security paperwork & procurement cadence

Contacts / owners
- Clearsky: Emma Sargent (product) + Procurement (procurement@clearskyhealth.com)
- Redwood: Jonas Weber (sales lead), Marissa Cole (solutions eng), Aditya Rao (security/ops)

Thanks — happy to adjust if you want the recap condensed into a decision checklist for Procurement.

Jonas
